market.category: NFL advanced player analytics and comparison apps
market.audience: NFL fans, fantasy and dynasty players, writers, and creators who need fast context on a player's value
market.problem: Box scores tell fans what happened, but not who was efficient, who is changing, or how a favorite fits the league
market.advantage: Football Next: StatScout turns advanced NFL metrics into scannable leaderboards, player profiles, recent movement, team context, following shortcuts, and side-by-side comparisons
market.competitive_context: It competes with score apps and dense desktop analytics pages. It wins by making EPA, percentile context, recent form, and fan-selected players readable in one mobile workflow

proof_points.claim: The Stats screen ranks fictional qualified quarterbacks by Pass Yds with visible position, season, metric, and sort controls
The player profile shows advanced percentile bars and the metric values behind a quarterback's ranking
The Trends screen surfaces quarterback movement with an honest week boundary and a selected recent window
The Chiefs team page keeps team context and roster paths in one real navigation destination
The Following board keeps a fan's team and selected players one tap away with season summaries
The player comparison screen aligns two quarterbacks and their season totals for a clear debate
The year comparison screen puts two available seasons into one metric-by-metric view

story.throughline: Move from a quick league scan to the context, movement, team view, and fan shortcuts that make every football debate easier

pitch.benefit: Find the players creating the most value without leaving the league board
pitch.problem: Box-score leaderboards hide efficiency and make advanced research slow
pitch.advantage: StatScout ranks qualified players with familiar production and a path to advanced context
pitch.proof: The literal Stats capture shows qualified quarterbacks ranked by Pass Yds with season, position, stat, and sort controls visible

frames.header: Know what makes a player elite

pitch.benefit: Understand the traits behind a player's ranking instead of relying on one headline stat
pitch.problem: One box-score line cannot explain efficiency, accuracy, pressure, and mistakes
pitch.advantage: StatScout turns a player profile into a percentile map with the underlying metric values beside it
pitch.proof: The literal profile capture shows grouped percentile bars and named metric values for the fictional Caleb Mercer profile

frames.header: See who is heating up right now
frames.story_focus: who is heating up right now

pitch.benefit: Spot players whose recent form is changing before season totals catch up
pitch.problem: Season totals move slowly and hide who has changed over the last few football weeks
pitch.advantage: StatScout compares recent windows and surfaces league-wide movement with a clear coverage boundary
pitch.header_advantage: who is heating up right now
pitch.proof: The literal Trends capture shows Heating up, a recent window, and quarterback movement through a named NFL week

frames.header: Scout your team in one view

pitch.benefit: Move from league-wide context to the team you watch most
pitch.problem: Team research gets scattered across player pages and disconnected totals
pitch.advantage: StatScout opens a favorite team with advanced, standard, and roster paths in one destination
pitch.proof: The literal Chiefs team capture shows the selected franchise, team context, and the app's Advanced, Standard, and Roster paths

frames.header: Keep your players one tap away

pitch.benefit: Turn a fan's team and favorite players into a quick personal stats board
pitch.problem: The players you care about most disappear inside a full league list
pitch.advantage: Following keeps team context and concise season summaries together, for free
pitch.header_problem: favorite players disappear in league lists
pitch.proof: The literal Following capture shows the favorite Chiefs shortcut and three followed fictional players with production summaries

frames.header: Settle the debate side by side

pitch.benefit: Make a fantasy, dynasty, or fan debate with the same context on both sides
pitch.problem: Separate stat pages make every player debate depend on mismatched context
pitch.advantage: StatScout aligns two players, their teams, and shared season totals in one comparison
pitch.proof: The literal comparison capture places Caleb Mercer and Mason Reed in parallel cards with aligned season totals

pitch.benefit: See where a player's production improved, declined, or stayed steady
pitch.problem: The latest season line hides the direction of a player's development
pitch.advantage: StatScout puts two available seasons into one metric-by-metric comparison
pitch.proof: The literal year comparison capture shows two available fictional seasons with aligned standard totals and winning-year cues
